overview:
Electric current is the flow of positive charges in a conducting metallic wire. 
Electric potential difference (V) is the work done to move a unit charge from one point to another.

Work done = Potential difference × Charge
= 12 V × 2 C
= 24 J Electric current is the flow of positive charges in a conductor. 
Electric circuit is a path through which electric current flows.

Electric potential difference (V) is measured by an instrument called voltmeter and is used to measure the work done in moving a charge across two points with a given potential difference.
revision_points: Work done to move a unit charge through a circuit is equal to the potential difference multiplied by the charge.
